breakfast.name: Banh Mi (Vietnamese Breakfast Sandwich)
breakfast.description: A beloved Vietnamese breakfast sandwich combining French colonial influences with Vietnamese ingredients - crusty bread filled with pâté, pickled vegetables, fresh herbs, and cilantro
instructions: Slice baguette lengthwise and lightly toast if desired
Spread mayonnaise on both sides of bread
Layer: pâté, sliced lemongrass pork, pickled vegetables, cucumber, chilies, and fresh herbs
Maintain proper ratio of filling to vegetables (approximately 1:1)
Do not overstuff
Slice sandwich in half if desired and serve immediately
Wrap in paper for easy eating
breakfast.notes: Balance of ingredients is crucial - too much filling makes it difficult to eat. The pickled vegetables provide essential tang and crunch
breakfast.fun_fact: Banh mi reflects Vietnam's colonial history through use of French baguettes and ingredients. It was eaten for breakfast more mornings than can be counted in Vietnam's Nha Trang
alternatives: Use grilled chicken instead of pork

lunch.name: Phở (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)
lunch.description: Iconic Vietnamese lunch - fragrant beef broth with rice noodles and tender beef. Combination of Vietnamese and French influences
ingredients: Fresh basil, cilantro, lime, chili for garnish
instructions: Char ginger and onion over open flame
In large pot, combine bones, charred ginger/onion, spices, fish sauce and water
Bring to boil, reduce heat, simmer 2-3 hours for deep flavor
Strain broth, season with fish sauce and salt
Cook rice noodles according to package
Arrange noodles in bowl, top with raw beef
Pour boiling broth over, beef will cook from heat
Serve with garnishes on side
lunch.notes: Long simmering time essential for rich broth flavor. Can prepare broth day ahead
lunch.fun_fact: Phở became iconic Vietnamese lunch, combination of Vietnamese and French influences from colonial era

dinner.name: Vietnamese Phở (Beef Noodle Soup with Aromatic Broth)
dinner.description: Beef noodle soup with fragrant aromatic broth - Vietnam's national dinner
ingredients: Garnishes: fresh basil, mint, cilantro, lime wedges, sliced chilies, thinly sliced white onion, scallions, bean sprouts, hoisin and sriracha sauce
instructions: Parboil bones 5-10 minutes; rinse and scrub under cold water
Char onion, ginger, shallots directly over flame 3-4 minutes per side
Add bones to large pot with 3.5 liters water; bring to boil
Reduce to gentle simmer; skim foam for first 30 minutes
Add charred vegetables and spices; maintain gentle simmer
Cook 6-8 hours for rich flavor (minimum 3 hours)
Add beef brisket after 2 hours; cook until tender
Strain broth through fine sieve; season with fish sauce and rock sugar
Cook pho noodles according to package directions; drain
Slice beef brisket thinly
Arrange noodles in bowls; top with beef; ladle hot broth over
Serve with garnish platter on the side
dinner.notes: Long slow cooking is essential for depth of flavor
dinner.fun_fact: Influenced by French pot-au-feu but distinctly Vietnamese

dinner.name: Ca Kho To (Braised Fish in Clay Pot)
dinner.description: Vietnamese braised fish in caramelized sauce - simple and delicious
ingredients: 500g catfish or snakehead fish, cut into thick chunks
2 tablespoons caramel sauce (or make from sugar and water)
instructions: Make caramel: heat 2 tablespoons sugar in pot until melted and golden (don't stir, just watch)
Carefully add 1 tablespoon water (caramel will sizzle)
Or use pre-made caramel sauce
Heat oil in clay pot or heavy skillet over medium heat
Add garlic slices and ginger slices, cook until fragrant (1 minute)
Add fish chunks, arrange in single layer
Pour caramel sauce, fish sauce, water over fish
Add whole chilies
Bring to gentle simmer (don't boil - fish will become tough)
Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes until fish is cooked through
The sauce should reduce slightly and become silky
Season with black pepper
Transfer to serving dishes, pour sauce over
Garnish with fresh dill
Serve with steamed rice
dinner.notes: Fish must simmer gently - not boil. Traditional cooking in clay pot adds flavor
dinner.fun_fact: Ca Kho To is a beloved Vietnam comfort food, often made at home rather than in restaurants
